subject: polygon with multiple parts in leaflet Map

messages.author: c593765222db4c71
messages.subject: polygon with multiple parts in leaflet Map
parts:
Hi All:

I am trying to create a US state map with leaflet in shiny. For the states with several separated parts(e.g. Washing State), I can't plot them with the same layerID. 
Here is my example: http://jianhua.shinyapps.io/leafletState/

If you zoom in to Washing State, you can find that it is plotted as several polygons with separated IDs as:
"washington:san juan island", "washington:lopez island","washington:orcas island", "washington:whidbey island", "washington:main"  

My purpose is to tread all of these separate parts as one entity? Is it possible to do that in shiny-leaflet?

Thanks for any suggestion.

Jianhua

messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Re: polygon with multiple parts in leaflet Map
parts:
Did you see the second post by Harri Hytönen in this thread?:

Actually solution is already in the function, in binding.js comment you can find out that you should just add null value before every new polygon. We did solve this problem also that way that we made our own function that can read list of polygons and show them on map.

messages.subject: Re: polygon with multiple parts in leaflet Map
parts:
yes, I can match the hover event with the ID's I want. For example, when I hover on Michigan.North, I can manage to return both Michigan.North and Michigan.South. 
But there are problems when I try to add both Michigan.North and Michigan.South to the map and highlight them. 

Here is the code for my app:
server.R:

library(leaflet)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(maps)
library(ggplot2)

rm(list = ls())
states <- map("state", plot=FALSE, fill=TRUE)
states$names <- gsub(':', '.', states$names ) 
statesDF <- fortify(states, region = 'id')
eachState <- split(statesDF, statesDF$region)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  map <- createLeafletMap(session, "map")
  observe({if (is.null(input$map_click)) {
      return()
    }
  })
  
  # session$onFlushed is necessary to delay the drawing of the polygons until
  # after the map is created
  session$onFlushed(once= T, function() {    
    map$addPolygon(states$y, states$x, states$names,
      lapply(brewer.pal(7, "Set1"), function(x) {
        list(fillColor = x)
      }),
      list(fill=T, fillColor="#800026", fillOpacity=.6, 
        stroke=TRUE, opacity=1, color="white", weight=1.5, dashArray = '3' 
      )
    ) 
  })
  
  observe({   
    # mouseover event (eventOver)
    # when the pointer is over a state, highlight that state and 
    # show information. layerID of addPolygon should be set as "sameID"
    # or any other name, so that the previou states are not highlighted.
    
    # when the highlighted state polygon is added, the eventOver$id will be 
    # updated to 's' (this is weird!). In order to avoid capturing the 
    # highlited state, set return() when eventOver$id == 's'. 
    eventOver <- input$map_shape_mouseover
    if (is.null(eventOver)||eventOver$id == 's') {
      return()
    }
    
    stateOver <- eachState[[eventOver$id]]
    map$addPolygon(stateOver$lat, stateOver$long, 'sameID') 
    output$eventOverInfo <- renderPrint({(eventOver$id)})    
  })
})

ui.R:
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  textOutput('eventOverInfo'),
  
  # create a div to contain leaflet Map, so that I can use percentage to 
  # control the heigth of the map
  # or else the heigth must be absolute px value (e.g. 500)
  div(class = 'mapContainer',
    leafletMap(
      "map", width = "100%", height = "100%",
      initialTileLayer = "http://{s}.tiles.mapbox.com/v3/jianhua1122.j5f28jda
      /{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
      initialTileLayerAttribution = NULL,
      options=list(
        center = c(40, -98.85),
        zoom = 4)
    )    
  ),
  
  tags$head(tags$style("
    .mapContainer {
      position: fixed;
      top: 50px;
      left: 0;
      right: 0;
      bottom: 0;
      overflow: hidden;
      padding: 0;
    }
  "))     
))

As you can see from the code, in order to avoid highlighting the previous states hovered over, the ID for the highlighted polygons should be set as "sameID". In this way, only the current state being hovered is highlighted. 
When the polygon has two parts, they can't share the "sameID". As a result, only the last part can be highlighted. 

This problem may be solved by highlighting the matched IDs directly, instead of adding the highlighted polygons as a new layer. But I can't find any function to highlight a polygong in leaflet. Maybe it is available in javascript code. 

Thanks for any input.

Jianhua
